results.description: Innovation S5: evidence-request policies on SYNTHETIC JSON-only cases with a hidden latent truth. Replaces the circular 'next-best-evidence top-1 vs resolving document' headline.

design.extraction: oracle: truth.oracle_extraction through the real checks and contradiction builder, with the oracle page text scanned for embedded instructions (no OCR, no PDF)

held_out_family.chosen: 2026-10-14, before any simulation was run (the Phase 4 spec's example)
held_out_family.rule: cases containing it were never simulated during development (development-split cases with it are never simulated); test-split cases with it are reported only under held_out_family
held_out_family.disclosure: the engine's detection of this problem (open_items_insurance.claims_history_items) was written and unit-tested by the engine build on other generated packets (seed 4040) before the simulator existed; the hold-out covers simulator development and every simulation result

policies.voi: highest nonzero VOI first; stop when no open request has a VOI above zero (innovation S5 rule)
policies.voi_lookahead: voi, then the zero-VOI request with the highest nonzero lookahead value (an addition)
policies.checklist: every open request in the fixed severity order of evidence.open_items.PROBLEM_ORDER (the catalog has no severity field)
policies.random: every open request in a seeded shuffled order
policies.oracle: knows the truth: cheapest cost-weighted request sequence that reaches the full-information recommendation (exhaustive uniform-cost search over request orders; only cases with at most 4 open requests at the start)

design.headline_policy: voi (the specified S5 stopping rule); voi_lookahead is reported as an addition

priors_variants.documented: template priors of config/resolution_templates.yaml (NOT the distribution the latent truths come from: see diagnostics.latent_vs_prior)
priors_variants.latent_x0.5: prior of the generator's latent option (the option the cause implies or nearest the hidden value; not drawn from the priors) x0.5, renormalized
priors_variants.latent_x1.5: prior of the generator's latent option x1.5, renormalized; where the documented prior of that option is below its latent share, this moves the priors TOWARD the truths
priors_variants.latent_removed: the generator's latent option removed from the option set, renormalized
priors_variants.empirical_dev: development-split latent shares, UNSMOOTHED: every option's prior is the share of development-split problems of its resolution template whose latent option it was (design.empirical_dev_priors). Options never latent there (some templates have only 4 development problems) get no prior and leave the set, which removes the TRUE option of some test problems (diagnostics.latent_without_prior.empirical_dev): for those problems this variant acts like latent_removed. NOT a correct-prior reference. A template without development problems keeps the documented priors
priors_variants.empirical_dev_smoothed: development-split latent counts with add-one (Laplace) smoothing: (count + 1) / (development problems of the template + its number of options) (design.empirical_dev_smoothed_priors); every option keeps a prior above zero, so none leaves the set. An estimate a practitioner could make from past cases
priors_variants.oracle_shares: in-sample ORACLE reference: priors equal to the latent shares of the evaluated group itself (test_main, held_out_family or development; design.oracle_shares_priors). Options never latent in the group leave the set, but the true option of every problem in the group keeps a prior above zero. No real underwriter has these priors: the row shows what the VOI policy does when its template-level priors match the truths

empirical_dev_priors.what: latent share per resolution template and option on the development split (the empirical_dev variant's priors), measured before any test case was simulated
empirical_dev_priors.smoothing: none: an option never latent on the development split gets no prior and leaves the set

empirical_dev_smoothed_priors.what: the empirical_dev_smoothed variant's priors, from the same development-split counts
empirical_dev_smoothed_priors.smoothing: add-one: (latent count + 1) / (development problems of the template + its options)

oracle_shares_priors.what: the oracle_shares variant's priors: the latent shares of each reporting group's own cases (an in-sample oracle reference, not available to a real underwriter)

design.case_cap: innovations.md S5 caps each case at 4 open items with 3 resolutions each. The resolution templates comply (2 or 3 options each), but the cases are NOT capped: the generator plants every problem its seeded draw gives, so some cases carry 5 planted problems and start with 5 open requests (diagnostics.planted_problems and the open_requests_at_start counts). Those cases are simulated like the others; only the oracle is not computed on them (it brute-forces request orders only up to 4 open requests).

metrics.requests_per_case: number of requests the policy made
metrics.cost_weighted_requests_per_case: sum of the catalog cost weights of those requests
metrics.zero_value_requests_per_case: requests whose VOI was 0 just before (under the variant's priors) and whose reveal did not change the recommendation
metrics.decision_error_rate: share of cases whose final recommendation differs from the full-information recommendation (every planted problem revealed)
metrics.requests_to_stable_when_reached: requests after which the recommendation equals the full-information recommendation and stays; cases ending on another recommendation are left out

reading_notes: The voi policy only makes requests whose VOI is above zero, so its zero-value request count is 0 by construction; the comparison is how many zero-value requests the other policies make.

Scaling the latent option's prior by 0.5 or 1.5 keeps every prior above zero, so it cannot change WHICH requests have a VOI above zero, only their values and order; for the voi policy, differences between the documented, x0.5 and x1.5 rows come only from the order of several nonzero requests. Removing the latent option can change which requests have value. voi_lookahead also depends on which option is most likely.
Checklist, random and oracle make the same requests under every priors variant; only the VOI they are valued at, and so the zero-value count, can change.

The full-information recommendation reveals every planted problem. A planted problem that no open item stands for cannot be requested by any policy; decision_error_rate_when_every_planted_problem_detected leaves those cases out.

requests_to_stable_when_reached averages only the cases where the run ends on the full-information recommendation, so its case set differs between policies; the paired comparison uses the cases both reached.

The oracle stops at the first state whose recommendation equals the full-information recommendation. That state need not be the full-information state: when a planted problem is undetected, another open problem can give the same recommendation, so 'oracle reached' does not mean every problem was revealed.

The full-information recommendation is what the SYNTHETIC reference policy (agent/policy.py) gives once every planted problem is revealed; it is the benchmark here, not a claim about the right lending or underwriting decision.

Latent truths do not follow the documented priors (diagnostics.latent_vs_prior): the generator takes the option the cause implies or the nearest one, so for several families one option is latent in every case and another never. The 'documented' rows are therefore not a correct-prior baseline, and the x0.5 / x1.5 rows measure robustness around priors that are already wrong (x1.5 can move a family toward its truth). Three table variants replace the priors with measured latent shares, so, unlike x0.5 / x1.5, they CAN change which requests have a VOI above zero. empirical_dev uses the development split's shares UNSMOOTHED: an option never latent on a small development sample gets no prior, so for some test problems the true option is removed (diagnostics.latent_without_prior counts them); it is an estimate with that defect, not a correct-prior reference. empirical_dev_smoothed is the same estimate with add-one smoothing (no option removed). oracle_shares is the correct-prior reference: the evaluated group's own shares, which no real underwriter has and which never remove a problem's true option.

innovations.md S5 caps each case at 4 open items with 3 resolutions each. The resolution templates comply (2 or 3 options each), but the cases are NOT capped: the generator plants every problem its seeded draw gives, so some cases carry 5 planted problems and start with 5 open requests (diagnostics.planted_problems and the open_requests_at_start counts). Those cases are simulated like the others; only the oracle is not computed on them (it brute-forces request orders only up to 4 open requests).

A reveal applies the generator's latent substitutions, which are not always the template option the engine values: insurance problems that change the claims of the latent world also set the stated claim count and total incurred to the true history (diagnostics.coupling). Revealing such a problem can therefore change the recommendation although the engine's own option for it did not (a VOI of 0 followed by a change), and in the held-out family it can remove the claims-history finding without the claims-history request; the cases where one coupled reveal alone does so are listed in diagnostics.coupling.held_out_family.

The held-out family's cases carry more co-planted problems than the main test split (diagnostics.planted_problems): part of its larger VOI decision error is the myopia of a one-step score on several co-occurring problems, not a family-specific weakness. decision_errors_by_kind splits every policy's errors into undetected planted problems, voi stops with every open request at VOI 0, and other.

Above $500,000 every credit case carries the amount-driven missing cpa_reviewed_financials document (latent always provided_consistent); diagnostics.structural_cpa reports those cases apart from the rest of the credit test split.

headline.group: test split without the held-out family, all lines, documented priors
headline.comparison: voi minus checklist, per case, paired bootstrap (1,000 resamples, seed 42)

latent_without_prior.note: planted problems whose TRUE option a table variant's priors leave out (the variant then acts like latent_removed for that problem), per group; counted whether or not an open item stands for the problem

structural_cpa.note: credit test cases (held-out family excluded) with the amount-driven missing cpa_reviewed_financials document, summarized apart from the other credit test cases

not_claimable: real time or cost savings (cost weights and priors are planning assumptions)
that the VOI score is optimal or an economic model
extraction accuracy (the simulator uses the generator's oracle extraction)
anything about real applications: every case is SYNTHETIC
